relevance_note: Cohort paper with a per-patient table of 24 individuals with SSADHD and their biallelic ALDH5A1 genotypes: "Demographics, molecular genotype, clinical characteristics, and laboratory findings of patients with SSADHD in our cohort."
method_note: Table 1 (24 patients as rows; Case # column of bare numbers) was transcribed by a Python script that reads the rows from the paper file; I checked its output against the table. Labels: the text refers to these people as 'Case <n>' (e.g. 'Case 2', 'Cases 11 and 13', 'case 22', 'Cases 17–24'), so rule 1 gives 'Case <n>' for all 24. Cases 1–16 are the BG-BCM cohort, Cases 17–24 the SSADHD Biobank. Footnotes mark Cases 11 and 13 (a) and Cases 14 and 15 (b) as full siblings; Case 11 is the younger brother of Case 13. No family labels are printed. Age (y) column = age at genetic testing or sample collection, recorded as age at last evaluation. Mother of Case 2 (healthy, untested), the in-utero-demised twin of Case 13, and the father of Case 13 (carrier of a 12q22.2 deletion only) were not given rows. Zygosity: Table 1 lists Allele 1 and Allele 2 without a zygosity term; zygosity is recorded only where the text states it (Case 2 'compound heterozygous'; Case 13 'confirmed to be in trans'). Identical alleles (Cases 1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 20, 22, 23) get one variant row each with zygosity not reported. Biobank urine GHB values recorded as elevated against the printed normal value 0–7 mmol/mol creatinine. Group statements by age group (pediatric/adult metabolite elevations) were not assigned to individuals; only statements naming cases were used. Case 13's 'aggression', 'sleep disturbances' and 'self-injurious behaviors' are excluded from Case 11's sentence 'much like his sister, never had ...' (inferred from group statement). Case 13's globus pallidus 'increased signal' does not name the sequence (T2), so the checklist MRI item stays not reported for her; the MRI was first read as normal and later reinterpreted. Contradictions/inconsistencies in the paper: (1) text says 'four individuals harbored homozygous' variants among the 16 BG-BCM cases, but Table 1 shows identical alleles for five (Cases 1, 3, 4, 5, 7); (2) c.1323dup is p.Pro442AlafsTer19 for Case 6 but p.Pro442AlafsTer18 for Case 21; (3) '16 individuals' vs 'identified 14 individuals with biallelic variants' (Cases 11 and 13 sequenced elsewhere); (4) succinamic acid elevations attributed to 'Supplementary Table S3', which elsewhere is the novel-variant table. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper does not say any patient was published before.
